The Corvenden entry does the harder thing: it records the hit against the note's own rejection standard rather than around it — 'the rejection list below turns away Sallowby, Casterly, Vantry and Brenlow for exactly this class of collision, so by the criteria stated here Corvenden would have been rejected at adoption had the hit been found, and it was not found until 2026-08-25' — and then gives three keep-grounds that are each independently checkable: law 16's trigger is a related-field bearer (a fictional moor is not one), nothing in the unit is attributed to Hunter's book, and a rename would force a full re-gate. That last one is true and I verified it: Corvenden occurs in the Q2 stem ('the way Vivienne Corvenden tunes a bell'), in Q4/A ('Mildly persuaded by Corvenden') and in Q4/D ('Corvenden's objection'), so a rename is a stem-and-option edit, not a metadata edit. The Larrowden/Harrowden near-miss I logged as an advisory is also absorbed into the note, correctly scoped as 'a distinct string with nothing attributed to it'. The one residual blanket negative, 'Larrowden and Ockthorne returned no bearer in any field on either run', is now framed as what the two runs returned rather than as a fact about the world, which is the correct epistemic form, and my run reproduces it.

resolutions.evidence: The A paragraph now opens 'A = direction lean, hedged in form – and it is the STANCE clause that falsifies it, not the evidential one. That is a stronger teaching payload than the fix I proposed: it hands the student the strongest version of their own objection and shows why it does not save the option.
